summary: The PR removes the check for `user.address` in `getUserCity`, introducing a runtime `TypeError` risk when a user object is missing an `address` property or when `address` is null/undefined.

findings.title: Unsafe property access on potentially missing `user.address`
findings.description: Removing the `if (!user.address)` guard clause causes `getUserCity` to throw a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')` whenever `user.address` is undefined or null. Optional chaining should be used if simplifying the function.
findings.verificationHypothesis: If a user object without an `address` property (e.g., `{ id: 1 }`) or with `address: null` is passed to `getUserCity`, the function will throw a `TypeError` instead of returning `null`.

suggestedReproduction.preconditions: `user` object is passed without an `address` key.
suggestedReproduction.suspiciousBehavior: Function throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')`.
